amendments.rule: **A waw the ASV renders by *also* takes it, wherever in the clause the ASV puts it.** This is rule 14's list — *but*, *then*, *or*, *now* — with the one member that keeps tempting an `added`. English writes *also* postpositively, after the fronted subject or between subject and verb — *Thy gates* ***also*** *shall be open*, *Thou shalt* ***also*** *suck the milk of the nations*, *I will* ***also*** *make thy officers peace* — so the word does not stand where the waw stands, and the unit is discontinuous under rule 25 rather than broken. Distance from the waw is not evidence against it, exactly as in rule 35. The corpus aligns a waw to *also* in 33 units across 21 chapters, so where a waw is present this is settled and the note need not hedge it. **But read whether a waw is present at all before placing the word.** Where no waw stands in the clause, no morpheme licenses the *also* and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30: `אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַשְׁאִיר לְךָ` → *that also shall not leave thee* has only the relative, the negative and the verb, and the *also* answers to none of them. Do not fold such an *also* into the relative, the negative or the verb to avoid the `added`, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* — the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. **And a waw on which the ASV has already spent a connective of its own is in the same position as an absent one.** Where the ASV recasts the waw's clause and writes a coordinator or a subordinator for it at that clause's left edge, that word is the waw's rendering under rules 14 and 55, and a further *also* standing in the same clause answers to no morpheme and is `added`: `וְלֹא־תָקִיא הָאָרֶץ אֶתְכֶם` → ***that*** *the land vomit not you out* ***also*** gives *that* to the waw and leaves the *also* `added`. Count the clause's connectives against the morphemes that could carry them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s and rule 52 counts its function words: a waw holding an English word of its own is not a home for a second one. Two limits. This does not reach the pair rule 55 governs, where a coordinator and a subordinator written together at the clause's left edge are one rendering of a single waw, nor rule 14's correlative pair, where *both … and*, *either … or* or *neither … nor* is one connective the ASV has written in two words; in each of those the two English words are one rendering rather than a second one. And it does not reach rule 25's distributed repetition, where the ASV rewrites one and the same connective over coordinated clauses.
amendments.why: LEV.18.28 is the case rule 51 had not considered. Its waw is present, so the rule's existing test — *read whether a waw is present at all* — points a later pass at that waw, but the ASV had already spent *that* on the recast clause (`וְלֹא־תָקִיא` → *that the land vomit not you out also*), and giving one waw both *that* and *also* would violate the count rules 42, 52, 29 and 33 apply everywhere else. The added clause narrows rule 51 where it stands rather than leaving the over-broad sentence for whoever reads it first, and it is written as an application of the count principle the contract already has. The two limits are stated because rule 55's *and that* / *and when* and rule 14's correlative pairs are both one rendering in two words and must not be read as a second word on a spent waw; the corpus's waw table (that 434, and that 22, so that 56, and when 40, both and 22, also 199) shows those groups and shows no waw carrying a subordinator and an *also* together.

conventions: Determiner precedence in this chapter, for a determiner the ASV writes once for a whole phrase: the morpheme that is itself what the word says takes it, and any other determiner morpheme in the phrase goes unrepresented. For any: a present כֹּל takes it (18.23 בְכָל־בְּהֵמָה any beast, 18.24, 18.26, 18.29), the partitive מִן taking only its own of; with no כֹּל standing, the partitive מִן takes the whole any of, headed on of (18.21 מִזַּרְעֲךָ any of thy seed, 18.30 מֵחֻקּוֹת any of these abominable customs), since the following noun already carries a determiner of its own and cannot be what the any determines; with neither morpheme present, the supplied any joins the noun's unit under rule 15 (18.23 אִשָּׁה any woman). For these: a written אֵלֶּה takes it and both articles of the phrase are unrepresented (18.26, 18.27, 18.29), while with no demonstrative written the article itself takes the these standing before the phrase (18.30 הַתּוֹעֵבֹת these ... abominable).

Supplied English connectives across the chapter: the word goes to a waw standing in the clause where one is present and has not already been spent, and is added where none is. Rendered on a waw: even (18.7, 18.29), or (18.17), therefore (18.5, 18.25, 18.26, 18.30), neither ... nor as one correlative pair (18.26), that (18.28), and that (18.30). Added: the appositional even of 18.9 and 18.10, where the clause holds neither a waw nor an object marker for it to rest on (rule 16); the conditional if of 18.5, the protasis writing no conjunction at all while אֲשֶׁר already holds its which (rule 55); and the also of 18.28, where the verse's one waw has already been spent on that. Do not fold any of these into a neighbouring noun, negative or verb to avoid the added.

The idiom נָתַן שְׁכֹבֶת (18.20, 18.23) is divided so that the finite verb carries the whole English finite verb — thou shalt lie, with auxiliary and subject pronoun under rule 17 — even though the ASV's lie recasts give. שְׁכֹבֶת then takes whatever single word is left for it (carnally at 18.20) and is unrepresented where the ASV writes none (18.23), as are its suffix in both verses and the לְזָרַע phrase of 18.20 (rule 40). The competing reading, which puts lie on the noun and leaves the verb only thou shalt, is what BSB's four disagreements in these two verses reflect.

In the kinship chains of 18.8–18.17 the ASV's one relational of goes to the rectum of the outermost construct and every inner rectum is rendered as an English possessive, whatever the depth of the chain: עֶרְוַת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיךָ → The nakedness of thy father's wife gives of ... wife to אִשָּׁה and father's to אָב (18.8), and the three-level עֶרְוַת בַּת־אֵשֶׁת אָבִיךָ → of thy father's wife's daughter gives of ... daughter to בַּת with wife's and father's inside it (18.11). The outer construct עֶרְוָה takes the supplied the under rule 29, and the unit holding the of is discontinuous around the English possessives under rule 25.

report: All 49 candidate lemma groups read end to end, together with the full verse dump. No cross-verse split found: every multi-treatment bucket is either plain ASV variation (הוּא your/you, אֶל to/unto/with, בְּ in/with/when/as long as, עַל besides/upon, כֹּל any/all) or licensed by a difference in what stands in the source.

שְׁכֹבֶת is the only bucket carrying a status difference (18.20 carnally, 18.23 unrepresented). It is licensed: the finite נָתַן keeps 'thou shalt lie' in both verses under rule 17, and 18.23 writes no second English word for the noun to hold. Its suffix, and the לְזָרַע phrase of 18.20, go unrepresented on the same ground (rule 40).

The 'any' group is a hierarchy, not a split: a present כֹּל takes the word (18.23, 24, 26, 29); with no כֹּל the partitive מִן takes 'any of' headed on 'of' (18.21, 30); with neither, the bare noun takes it under rule 15 (18.23 'any woman'). Word order settles 18.21 and 18.30 decisively — 'thy seed' and 'these ... customs' already carry a determiner, so an 'any' standing before 'of' cannot be the noun's.

The nine added units, which the lemma table is blind to, follow one practice: a connective goes to a waw standing in the clause and not already spent, and is added otherwise. even to the waw at 18.7 and 18.29; even added at 18.9 and 18.10, where neither a waw nor an object marker stands; if added at 18.5; also added at 18.28. The supplied objects (18.18 'to her', 18.21 'them', 18.29 'them'), the supplied 'through the fire' of 18.21 and the supplied possessive of 18.6 (עֶרְוָה absolute, no suffix) are consistently added as well.

18.26's 'neither ... nor' is one correlative pair on the waw rather than rule 14's transfer of the opening word to a present negative: that clause's לֹא already holds its own 'not', and rule 14's own counting sentence is what resolves three English words against two morphemes. The corpus's 22 'both ... and' units on a bare waw support a correlative pair resting on a single connective morpheme.

BSB: all 18 disagreements are documented convention differences on function morphemes — the lamed of לֵאמֹר (rule 27), object markers (rule 16), articles the ASV writes no the for (rules 22, 29), the apodosis waw of 18.5 and the connectiveless waw of 18.22 (rule 14), the second אִישׁ of the distributive at 18.6 (rule 22), and the שְׁכֹבֶת/לְזָרַע cluster the ASV recasts away. None is a genuine error and no accepted edge should move for the aggregate.

One amendment returned. LEV.18.28 is the case rule 51 had not considered: a waw is present but the ASV had already spent 'that' on the recast clause, so rule 51's 'read whether a waw is present at all' would have sent a later pass to give one waw both words. Rule 51 is narrowed in place; rules 14 and 55 are expressly left untouched.
